name: upstream_status
summary: The upstream did not return a success status, so there is no completed exchange to record.
trigger: The response phase completed and the upstream status was anything other than a success.
grounding: A turn is a completed exchange with a provider; an error response is a record of one failing to happen. Capturing them would put failed requests in the same log as conversations and leave every consumer to re-derive the difference — including the deriver, which projects rows into a conversation tree. Any implementation sees the status, so any implementation can apply this, which is what makes it contract rather than plumbing.
not_expressible: The status alone does not decide it: the reason is only reached once the response phase has completed, which is stream state rather than data. A case asserting status-to-outcome would pin the status test and silently claim the surrounding lifecycle it does not exercise.
notes: The two implementations currently disagree here — the gateway adapter captures only 200 and drops the rest; the client records upstream_status in metadata and captures regardless. Recorded in the README as a known divergence rather than repaired by this corpus.
